about: The 75 rows of Nemotron's first full run on the hero topics (127 pairs, 721 rows) that hero-findings-notes.md judged by hand: every numbers, contradiction and framing row, and the sample of 24 missing-fact rows (8 per topic, random.seed(4) over the rows in hero_agree.py's order).
label: real (real or plausible), false, or unclear (for a human, weak, partly there, or not settled by a search).

basis: 'notes' when hero-findings-notes.md names the row; 'working summary' when only the judge's working summary of the night names it; 'inferred' when neither does. The notes give the missing-fact sample as 10 real, 5 false and 9 unclear and name the five false rows; the working summary names four of the unclear ones. The split of the other 15 into 10 real and 5 unclear is rebuilt from the judge's searches, and which of missing_fact-01 and missing_fact-23 is the tenth real row could not be recovered.

recheck: where a search of the stored article (demo/hero_verify.py's database, 2026-11-14) contradicts the label. hero_score.py scores against label and prints a second table with the rechecks applied.

rows.quote_b: The Finns rose up in guerrilla fighting as far east as Frederikshamn (Finnish: Hamina) within the Old Finland province of Russia
rows.summary: The English passage states that Tuchkov left garrisons along his route, reducing his unit to 4,000 troops, and that Finns rose up in guerrilla fighting as far east as Frederikshamn/Hamina; the Finnish passage does not mention the 4,000-troop figure or the guerrilla uprising.
rows.label: real
rows.note: the Finnish mentions of Hamina are about other things

rows.quote_b: Sprengtporten suggested going on to an offensive during the winter since Finland would be mostly isolated when seas were frozen
rows.summary: The English passage states that Sprengtporten proposed a winter offensive because frozen seas would isolate Finland; the Finnish passage does not mention this.
rows.label: unclear
rows.note: Finnish has Sprengtporten as an adviser; not settled by a search

recheck.label: false
recheck.note: Finnish has 'hän oli jo aiemmin suositellut venäläisille talvista sotaa Ruotsia vastaan'

rows.quote_a: Työn Äänen tihutyön tekijöiksi ja tukijoiksi ilmoittautui Kosolan, Yrjö Nikulan, Vihtori Herttuan ja ilmajokelaisen pankinjohtajan Iivari Koiviston johdolla 72 miestä, jotka saapuivat 9. huhtikuuta joukolla Vaasaan maaherran luo
rows.quote_b: On April 4th seventy-two men publicly declared themselves responsible for the attack, but only the actual perpetrators and the main organizer, Yrjö Nikula, were charged
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates the 72 men's arrival in Vaasa to April 9, while the English passage dates their public declaration of responsibility to April 4.
rows.label: unclear
rows.note: for a human: 72 men, 9 April or 4 April

rows.quote_a: Tasavallan suojelulain voimassaolo tosin rajoitettiin viiteen vuoteen, koska myös RKP vaati sitä
rows.quote_b: Social Democrats were only willing to accept the law for a three year temporary period, which meant that the Act only received a simple majority and had to be voted on by the next parliament
rows.summary: The Finnish passage gives the Protection of the Republic Act a five-year duration; the English passage gives it a three-year temporary period.
rows.label: false
rows.note: two quantities: a law limited to five years against a party willing to accept three

rows.quote_a: Jo Lapuan Liike Ry:n perustamiskokouksessa marraskuussa 1930 oli julistettu sota sosiaalidemokratialle, jonka väitettiin olevan samaa juurta kommunismin kanssa
rows.quote_b: The movement originated in November 1929, after Finnish communist youth paraded in the conservative and religious town of Lapua enraged pro-White Guard locals, who subsequently attacked the performers physically
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates the Lapuan Liike Ry founding meeting to November 1930, while the English passage dates the movement’s origin to November 1929.
rows.label: false
rows.note: two events: a founding meeting of November 1930 against an origin in November 1929

rows.quote_a: Lapuan Liike Ry:n toiminta kiellettiin käytännössä jo 29. helmikuuta tasavallan suojelulain nojalla
rows.quote_b: After a trial, the Lapua Movement was banned on 21 November 1932 under the Protection of the Republic Act, which Lapua itself had worked to get passed
rows.summary: The Finnish and English passages give different dates for the banning of the Lapua Movement: 29 February 1932 in Finnish and 21 November 1932 in English.
rows.label: real
rows.note: ban date, 29 February or 21 November 1932

rows.quote_a: Den 7 juli demonstrerade rörelsen sin styrka genom att samla omkring 12 000 utvalda män till ett bondetåg till Helsingfors
rows.quote_b: The Peasant March gathered 12,600 men to Helsinki where they marched through the city, held speeches and sermons and were greeted by distinguished politicians and generals
rows.summary: The Swedish passage gives around 12,000 men at the Peasant March; the English passage gives 12,600.
rows.label: real
rows.note: 12,000 or 12,600 marchers

rows.quote_a: Efter den efterföljande rättegången, då 102 av rörelsens ledare fängslades, upplöstes Lapporörelsen
rows.quote_b: Wallenius and about 50 other leaders were sentenced to prison
rows.summary: The Swedish passage says 102 leaders were imprisoned after the trial, while the English passage says about 50 leaders were sentenced to prison.
rows.label: real
rows.note: 102 or about 50 leaders

rows.quote_a: Porvoon valtiopäivät oli kutsuttu koolle 22. maaliskuuta (J: 10. maaliskuuta), ja ne päätettiin 19. heinäkuuta (J: 7. heinäkuuta) 1809
rows.quote_b: During the Finnish War between Sweden and Russia, the four Estates of Russian-occupied Finland (nobility, clergy, burghers and peasants) were assembled in Porvoo (Borgå) by Tsar Alexander I, the new Grand Duke of Finland, between 25 March and 19 July 1809
rows.summary: Both give the Diet's start and end dates, but the opening date differs: Finnish gives 22 March (Old Style 10 March) while English gives 25 March; the closing date, 19 July, agrees.
rows.label: real
rows.note: the diet opened on 22 or 25 March

rows.quote_a: Aleksanteri I antoi hallitsijanvakuutuksensa 29. maaliskuuta 1809
rows.quote_b: Given at Borgå on the 15th/27th day of March in 1809
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates Alexander I's pledge to 29 March 1809, while the English passage dates it to 15/27 March 1809.
rows.label: false
rows.note: the day the pledge was given, 29 March, against the date written in the document, 15th/27th March; English has 29 March too

rows.quote_a: denne avgav sin regentsförsäkran den 29 mars 1809
rows.quote_b: Given in Borgå on the 15th/27th day of March in 1809
rows.summary: The Swedish passage dates the sovereign's pledge to 29 March 1809, while the English passage gives 15/27 March 1809.
rows.label: false
rows.note: as above

rows.quote_a: den 29 mars 1809
rows.quote_b: Given at Borgå on the 15th/27th day of March in 1809
rows.summary: The Swedish passage dates the sovereign’s pledge to 29 March 1809, while the English passage dates it to the 15th/27th of March 1809.
rows.label: false
rows.note: as above

rows.quote_a: Venäläiset ylittivät Ruotsin rajan viidestä kohtaa
rows.quote_b: Det ryska anfallet genomfördes med tre kolonner
rows.summary: The Finnish passage states that the Russians crossed the border at five places, while the Swedish passage states that the attack was carried out with three columns.
rows.label: unclear
rows.note: five crossing points against three columns

rows.quote_a: Ruotsin kuningaskuntaan julistettiin sotatila 3. maaliskuuta
rows.quote_b: The king was quite unprepared for the attack, especially as war was not declared until April
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates the declaration of war to 3 March, while the English passage says war was not declared until April.
rows.label: unclear
rows.note: state of war 3 March against 'war was not declared until April'

rows.quote_a: Klingspor käski noin 8000 miehen vahvuisen pääarmeijan vetäytyä
rows.quote_b: 7 000 man retirerade från Tavastehus norrut
rows.summary: The Finnish passage gives the main army retreating from Hämeenlinna as about 8,000 men, while the Swedish passage gives 7,000 men retreating from Tavastehus northwards.
rows.label: real
rows.note: about 8 000 or 7 000 men in the retreat

rows.quote_a: Prikaati vetäytyi Kuopiosta 15. päivä, muttei ollut ilmoittanut asiasta etuvartiostolle
rows.quote_b: In Savonia, Russians also advanced rapidly and took Kuopio on 16 March
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates the Kuopio retreat/battle to 15 March, while the English passage dates the Russian capture of Kuopio to 16 March.
rows.label: false
rows.note: compatible: the brigade left Kuopio on the 15th and the Russians took it on the 16th

rows.quote_a: Savon prikaati koostui 3 500 miehestä, ja sitä oli vastassa 6 500 venäläistä sotilasta
rows.quote_b: 7 000 man retirerade från Tavastehus norrut och den 4 000 man starka Savolaxbrigaden, under Johan Adam Cronstedt, retirerade mot Uleåborg österifrån
rows.summary: The Finnish passage states the Savonia brigade had 3,500 men, while the Swedish passage gives the Savolax brigade's strength as 4,000 men.
rows.label: real
rows.note: Savo brigade 3 500 or 4 000 men

rows.quote_a: joka kuljetti John Mooren alla toimivan 11 000 sotilaan vahvuisen armeijan
rows.quote_b: Had the king accepted the landing of 10,000 British troops in Scania, where the expeditionary force had been authorized to disembark, it would have enabled the Swedes to release at least 10,000 trained soldiers for the Finnish War
rows.summary: The Finnish passage gives the British force under John Moore as 11,000 soldiers, while the English passage gives the authorized landing force as 10,000 troops.
rows.label: false
rows.note: fi 11 000 under Moore against an English sentence about a hypothetical 10,000; English has 14,000 elsewhere

rows.quote_a: Toukokuun 1808 alussa Viaporin piiritetty linnoitus antautui venäläisille juuri Suomenlahden vapautuessa jäistä
rows.quote_b: The fortress surrendered on 6 May 1808 after prolonged negotiations with the Russians as the commanding officer Carl Olof Cronstedt and his council believed that resistance was futile
rows.summary: The Finnish passage dates the surrender to early May 1808, while the English passage gives the exact date of 6 May 1808.
rows.label: false
rows.note: compatible: 'early May' against 6 May

rows.quote_a: 3 600 venäläissotilaan voimin
rows.quote_b: deployed over 3,000 men
rows.summary: The Finnish passage gives 3,600 Russian soldiers at the landing, while the English passage gives over 3,000.
rows.label: false
rows.note: compatible: 3 600 against 'over 3,000'

rows.quote_a: Den svenska fältarmén räknade ca 17 000 man, varav ca 7 000 man förlades till fästningarna Sveaborg och Svartholm
rows.quote_b: About 21,000 Swedish troops were stationed in various fortresses in Finland, while the rest of his army was unable to leave southern Sweden for fear of Danish attack
rows.summary: The Swedish passage gives about 7,000 Swedish troops in the fortresses Sveaborg and Svartholm, while the English passage gives about 21,000 Swedish troops stationed in various fortresses in Finland.
rows.label: false
rows.note: sv 17 000 of whom 7 000 in two fortresses against en 21,000 in various fortresses

rows.quote_a: Nästan 7 000 man var förlagda till Sveaborg
rows.quote_b: a garrison of 6,000 men
rows.summary: The Swedish passage gives the Sveaborg garrison as almost 7,000 men, while the English passage gives it as 6,000 men.
rows.label: real
rows.note: Sveaborg garrison almost 7 000 or 6,000

rows.quote_a: Den ryska belägringen inleddes i medlet av mars 1808 och avslutades den 3 maj med Sveaborgs kapitulation
rows.quote_b: The fortress surrendered on 6 May 1808 after prolonged negotiations with the Russians as the commanding officer Carl Olof Cronstedt and his council believed that resistance was futile
rows.summary: The Swedish passage dates Sveaborg's capitulation to 3 May 1808, while the English passage dates the surrender to 6 May 1808.
rows.label: real
rows.note: Sveaborg surrendered 3 or 6 May

rows.quote_a: I maj ankom en brittisk hjälpkår om 14 000 man till Göteborg
rows.quote_b: Had the king accepted the landing of 10,000 British troops in Scania, where the expeditionary force had been authorized to disembark, it would have enabled the Swedes to release at least 10,000 trained soldiers for the Finnish War
rows.summary: The Swedish passage gives 14,000 men for the British force that arrived in Gothenburg, while the English passage gives 10,000 British troops authorized to land in Scania.
rows.label: false
rows.note: sv 14 000 under Moore against an English sentence about a hypothetical 10,000; English has 14,000 elsewhere

rows.quote_a: en kår om 1 000 man landsteg i ryssarnas rygg
rows.quote_b: Colonel Johan Bergenstråhle landed 1,100 Swedes just a few kilometers northeast of Vaasa on 25 June and managed to quickly advance to the town
rows.summary: The Swedish passage gives the Swedish landing force near Vaasa as 1,000 men, while the English passage gives it as 1,100.
rows.label: real
rows.note: 1 000 or 1,100 men landed at Vaasa
